gao-gaoreports-gao-07-162g: Government Auditing Standards, in its January 2007 revision, is GAO's own rulebook for audits of government work. The revision is numbered GAO-07-162G and dated January 31, 2007. It supersedes the 2003 revision. The hosted text carries the front matter and the full table of contents rather than every chapter in full. The contents map standards on ethics, independence, competence, and quality control. They also map field work and reporting standards for financial audits, attestation work, and performance audits.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-82g:
Auditors of federal books need one shared playbook. GAO-08-82G, dated October 1, 2007, is volume two of the Financial Audit Manual, issued as an exposure draft. GAO and a council of inspectors general keep the manual, which guides audits of federal financial statements.

The volume packs checklists and audit programs for testing compliance with key money laws. Named parts cover the Antideficiency Act, the Prompt Payment Act, pay systems, and retirement laws. Other parts guide work on related parties, shared dealings between agencies, and cost data. As a draft, it invites comment before final form. Auditors use it to keep agency audits uniform.
uslaw-usc-t2-s142g: Section 142g of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with pay for a tribunal's staff. The tribunal is the Copyright Royalty Tribunal named in the title. The Library of Congress is the body picked to do the pay work. It may work out the base pay of all tribunal staff. It may also pay that base pay out to the staff. The start date for the power is the 1st of October 1983. The pay work must follow a named pay section of Title 5.
